findings.title: Smoke spec header comment points at the wrong chart spec
findings.description: The updated comment says the live chart at "/" is "asserted in chart-render.spec.ts". That spec (unchanged from slice 102) navigates to `/__chart-harness` — the slice-102 test harness, not the product route. The live chart at "/" is asserted in the new `e2e/chart-live.spec.ts` (`page.goto('/')`). In the sentence's own context ("As of slice 103 '/' renders the LIVE chart… the chart itself is asserted in…"), the pointer is wrong and would send a future maintainer to the harness spec when the product chart regresses. Fix: reference `chart-live.spec.ts`.

findings.title: jsdom measured-rect stub duplicated verbatim across four test files
findings.description: `const MEASURED = { width: 1024, height: 640 }` plus `function measuredRect(): DOMRect { … } as DOMRect` is copy-pasted in `use-chart-provider.errors.test.tsx` (lines 30-43), `use-chart-provider.facade.test.tsx` (~lines 33-46), and `use-chart-provider.translation.test.tsx` (~lines 38-51), and the same literal is inlined inside the `measure` callback in `use-chart-provider.resize.test.tsx` (~lines 33-38). This diff introduces four copies of the same 10-line stub, while the same diff deliberately centralizes the provider spy and the render wrapper "so the suites share one convention rather than re-deriving a double each file" (its own words in `chart-provider-spy.ts`). That contradicts the project's DRY rule. Move `MEASURED`/`measuredRect` into `src/test/support/` (e.g. export from `chart-provider-spy.ts` or a small jsdom-stub module) and import in all four files.

findings.title: `react-hooks/refs` is disabled for the whole hook file; a line-level disable would be tighter
findings.description: The new config block disables `react-hooks/refs` for the entire 366-line `src/chart/use-chart-provider.ts`. The rationale comment is thorough and the construction is genuinely correct (I verified `buildChartOperations`/`series` only *store* closures that read refs — nothing reads `.current` during render, so the rule's finding is a transitive-analysis false positive). But a file-wide disable also silences the rule for any *future* ref-during-render read added anywhere in this complex file. `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/refs` on the two `useMemo` calls (facade + counter callbacks) would keep the suppression exactly as narrow as the false positive. Optional, but strictly better hygiene.

findings.title: Range-translation comment overstates when the effect activates
findings.description: The comment above the visible-range effect says the seam "activates the moment [initiative 120] adds the first series". The effect's dependency array is `[mount.ready, chart, range]` — series count is a ref read in the body, not a dependency — so adding the first series does **not** re-run the effect; the current/default range is only pushed on the *next* `range` change (or never, if range never changes after data lands). The behavior itself matches the tests ("applies the range once a series exists" works because `setRange` follows `addSeries`), so nothing is broken in this slice — but the comment should say activation is gated on having a series and triggered by a range change, or initiative 120's implementer may assume the default range applies automatically on first data load.

findings.title: "does not translate after unmount" test passes vacuously
findings.description: The test unmounts the tree rendered by `renderWithContexts`, which tears down *both* `Host` and the Context providers. The captured `symbolTimeframe().setRange` handle then calls `setState` on an already-unmounted provider — a no-op — so the context value can never change, the hook's effect can never re-run, and the assertion `setVisibleRange` not called is true by construction. The stated intent ("a late setter must not reach the destroyed chart") is never actually exercised. The real guard (facade calls dropped via `runGuarded`/`disposedRef` after teardown) is covered by the teardown-race tests in `use-chart-provider.errors.test.tsx`, but this test should either keep the provider mounted (unmount only `Host`) to be meaningful, or be removed in favor of those.

findings.title: Live-chart e2e samples pixels in a single shot right after canvas visibility
findings.description: `samplePanes` runs once, immediately after `expect(canvas).toBeVisible()` and two `boundingBox()` round-trips. The canvas becomes visible as soon as lightweight-charts appends it with a size (synchronously in `create`), but the background is painted on a later animation frame; a slow CI frame could interleave before the single `getImageData` read, making `expect(sample.mainPanePixel).toBe(hexToRgba(...))` (line 141) flaky. The resize spec's re-sample (line 167) is safe because the preceding `poll` guarantees a settled repaint. Consider wrapping the pixel assertion in `expect.poll` around `samplePanes` (CI's `retries: 2` currently masks this class of flake).

findings.title: A container that appears after first render never mounts the chart (no re-run, no error)
findings.description: The mount effect's deps are `[containerRef, setMountOutcome, runGuarded]` — the ref object's identity is stable, so if `containerRef.current` is `null` on first effect run (e.g. a conditionally rendered container) the effect no-ops and will **never** re-run when the element appears; the chart silently stays `ready: false` with no `error` and no retry. This cannot happen in this slice (`ChartRoute` renders the section unconditionally) and the param doc ("nothing happens while null") acknowledges the contract, but it's a latent trap for initiative 120, which will add routes sharing this hook. At minimum, the hook's doc comment should state that the container must exist on first mount; ideally the effect would observe the ref (e.g. a `useSyncExternalStore`-style check or a render-phase `null → element` transition) so a late container mounts instead of hanging.

findings.title: Hook file is 366 lines against the ~300-line guide
findings.description: Documented in the slice doc's Implementation Outcomes as a known, PM-approved overrun (the type surface and facade were already extracted; the remainder is one inseparable mount sequence). Noted for the record — no action required, but it's the file most likely to grow further as initiative 120 fills the indicator placeholder, so the extraction seam should be revisited rather than accepting a second overrun.

findings.title: Error funnel and teardown ordering correctly cover every post-mount provider path
findings.description: Verified by reading: `runGuarded` is the single funnel (ready/disposed guard + try/catch → `console.error` + `setOperationError`), the ResizeObserver callback routes through it (line ~250), subscription setup runs inside the mount try/catch so a mid-sequence throw tears down with `ready: false`, each disposer is pushed individually (the argument-evaluation leak is avoided and covered by a test), and teardown order is dispose → disconnect → destroy → null-ref with the `disposed` flag closing the queued-callback window (tested in `use-chart-provider.errors.test.tsx` "teardown race"). Every catch logs and either handles with a comment or completes teardown — compliant with the project exception rule.

findings.title: Harness gate is statically foldable and the e2e mode is wired end to end
findings.description: The gate uses direct `===` comparisons on `import.meta.env.MODE` (lines 44-45), which Vite constant-folds to `false` in a `production` build so the dead branch and the `ChartHarnessRoute` import are eliminated — the comment correctly explains why a runtime `.includes()` form would have shipped the harness (and the slice doc records the production-bundle grep that caught exactly that regression). `playwright.config.ts:41` passes `--mode e2e` to both `build` and `preview`, keeping the e2e artifact consistent with `chart-render.spec.ts`, which I confirmed still targets `/__chart-harness`.

findings.title: Typed seam is clean: no `any`, generic preserved, lifecycle not exposed
findings.description: Verified across the diff: no `any`/`as any` in any changed file (grep confirmed); `ChartOperations` is a typed subset of `IChartProvider` deliberately excluding `create`/`destroy` (asserted in the facade test); `getCapability` keeps its `<K extends CapabilityKey>` generic through the facade with a compile-time `expectTypeOf` check; `MountState`/`UseChartProviderResult` are fully typed with annotated returns on all exports; the two Contexts throw explicitly outside their providers (no silent default context), consistent with the project's no-silent-fallback rule.
